HowTo.title: How-to
HowTo.subtitle: How Linyup fits together, and how to get your studio up and running.
HowTo.conceptsIntro: Four building blocks power everything inside Linyup. Tap a block on the map — or a card below — to see what it does and how it connects.
HowTo.diagramAria: Map of how Linyup's core concepts connect
HowTo.diagramHint: Swipe the map — tap a block to learn more.

activities.label: Activities
activities.body: Activities are the catalogue of what you offer. Each one is either a class — a subject you schedule onto the calendar, like Judo Fundamentals — or an appointment: time with a specific person, booked from the availability they publish. An activity carries its own price and access rule (open to everyone, members only, or reserved for specific subscriptions), which is what makes it a distinct offering rather than a label.
terms: Class — a subject you schedule as sessions people book a seat in
Appointment — an offering booked from a person's published availability
Event — a separate format for one-offs like camps, workshops or exams
Access tier — who may book: open, members, or specific subscriptions

sessions.label: Classes & Appointments
sessions.body: This is the calendar itself — Tuesday's 7 pm class, not the class in general. Bookings connect people to it: one contact, one spot, one time.
sessions.compareIntro: Three shapes share the calendar. What separates them is who puts the time there:

compare.title: Class
compare.body: You schedule it. The session sits on the calendar with a set number of seats before anyone books, and people book a seat in it.

compare.title: Appointment
compare.body: Nothing exists until someone books. The provider (coach) publishes their availability — the windows they are free — and the session is created the moment a client takes one. Exclusive time: one booking per slot.

compare.title: Event
compare.body: A one-off with its own registration — a camp, a workshop, a grading. It stands on its own rather than being an instance of an activity.

terms: Session — one scheduled occurrence, whether you placed it or a booking created it
Availability — when a provider (coach) is free; appointments are booked out of it
Booking — a contact’s reserved spot
Event — a standalone happening with its own registration

subscriptions.label: Subscriptions & affiliations
subscriptions.body: Subscriptions are the recurring plans your members pay for — and they can do more than bill, because a plan can unlock exactly the activities it covers. Affiliations track belonging without money: whether someone is an active member, on trial or alumni. Together they answer two different questions about a person: what can they access, and how do they belong.
terms: Plan — a subscription type with its price and billing cycle
Access gating — an activity can require a subscription that covers it
Affiliation — a membership status independent of payment

contacts.label: Contacts
contacts.body: Contacts are the people side of Linyup — leads, trialists, members and alumni all live in one list. Everything else attaches to a contact: the subscriptions they hold, their affiliation status and the sessions they have booked. When someone books or signs up through one of your public pages, a contact is created or matched automatically.
contacts.funnelIntro: Contacts move through three acquisition stages. The stage only ever advances — it is a high-water mark, not a status you set back and forth:

funnel.label: Trial booked
funnel.meaning: They have reserved their first session but have not turned up yet.

funnel.label: Trial attended
funnel.meaning: They showed up. Marking the first attendance promotes them automatically.

funnel.label: Joined
funnel.meaning: They finished signup and are a member of the studio.

contacts.funnelNote: Someone can also arrive with NO stage at all — a shop purchase or a form submission captures a lead off the funnel. They join it at Trial booked on their first booking, or jump straight to Trial attended the first time they show up.
terms: Contact — one person's record, from first touch to long-time member
Subscription holder — a contact with an active plan
Affiliation status — how a contact belongs (member, trial, alumni)

publicPages.title: Public pages
publicPages.intro: Public pages are the surfaces people see without logging in — where your new contacts and bookings actually come from. Each is optional and switched on when you need it, so you only expose what your studio uses.

bioLink.name: Bio-link
bioLink.desc: Your link-in-bio landing page — one short URL that gathers your booking link, socials and key actions. The simplest thing to share on Instagram or in a bio.

website.name: Website
website.desc: A fuller studio site you build from blocks — hero, schedule, pricing, gallery and more — at your public address. Turn it on when a single bio-link isn't enough.

booking.name: Booking page
booking.desc: The public schedule anyone can book from. Visitors pick a class and a time, enter their details, and a contact plus a booking appear automatically.

shop.name: Shop
shop.desc: A storefront that gathers what you sell — subscriptions, products and courses — so people can buy without a back-and-forth. Appears once you have something to sell.

space.name: Member space
space.desc: The logged-in area for your members: their subscription, bookings, profile and the courses they can open. Their home base between visits.

appointments.name: Appointments
appointments.desc: Clients pick a coach, choose what they're booking and take a free time from that coach's published availability. Nothing sits on the calendar until they book. Separate from the class booking page, so appointments book cleanly.

kiosk.name: Kiosk
kiosk.desc: A fixed, low-chrome screen for an entrance tablet: today's schedule, a check-in QR and walk-in sign-up. What members and drop-ins see at the door.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.intro: Pricing pulls together three ideas that usually live in different places — what you offer, what you sell, and the benefits that connect them. Explore the map, browse a few common setups, then try it live with a fictional visitor.

map.title: How pricing fits together
map.intro: Four pieces connect to produce one price. Tap a block on the map — or a card below — to see what it covers.
map.diagramAria: Map of how pricing fits together
map.diagramHint: Swipe the map — tap a block to learn more.

offer.label: What you offer
offer.body: Everything a visitor can book or buy: classes and appointments on your schedule, online courses, and shop items. Each one carries its own base price — or none at all — before any benefit changes it.
items: Classes — scheduled sessions people book a seat in
Appointments — a provider's time, booked from availability
Online courses — self-paced lessons, sold or included
Shop items — products and gift cards

sell.label: What you sell
sell.body: The things people pay for once or on a schedule: memberships, class packs and gift cards. Holding one of these is exactly what a member benefit checks for.
items: Memberships — recurring plans, optionally capped per week
Class packs — one-time credits, spent per booking
Gift cards — a prepaid balance, redeemable anywhere

benefits.label: Member benefits
benefits.body: One rule on an offering says what holding a chosen plan changes about its price. There are three shapes: included for free, a percentage off, or a fixed member price. Absent — everyone simply pays the base price.
items: Included — holders book for free (a pack spends one credit instead)
Percentage off — a reduced price for holders
Fixed member price — a flat price that replaces the base one

preview.label: The price preview
preview.body: Pick anyone — a guest, a member, or a specific plan — and Offer → Pricing shows exactly what they'd pay for every class, appointment, course and product, using the same logic as checkout.
items: One persona at a time — guest, member, or a specific plan
Every offering priced the same way real checkout would
Health checks flag pricing that doesn't add up

recipes.title: I want to…
recipes.intro: Common pricing setups, each with how it works, where to set it up, what members see, and how to check it before you switch it on.

sell-membership.how: Create a subscription type under Offer → Plans with one or more prices (monthly, annual). Mark it public so it appears in your shop. Members buy it there and are billed automatically.
sell-membership.see: Members see it on your public shop's Memberships tab and in their Space.
sell-membership.check: Pick that plan's persona on Offer → Pricing.

limit-weekly.chip: Cap a plan at N classes per week
limit-weekly.how: On the subscription type, set a usage limit like 3 per week. Covered bookings count against a weekly allowance (resets Monday); when it's used up, the member can still pay the drop-in price — at their member rate if you set one.
limit-weekly.see: Members see "2 of 3 left" style coverage; the 4th booking offers the drop-in.
limit-weekly.check: The persona picker has an "allowance used up" switch.

drop-in.how: On a gated class, enable Drop-in with a price. Anyone not covered — guests included — can book that single class by paying.
drop-in.see: Members covered by the class book free; everyone else sees the drop-in price at booking.
drop-in.check: Compare the Guest persona with a member persona.

member-rate.how: Inside the class's drop-in section, add a member rate: holders of chosen plans pay a percentage off or a fixed price instead of the full drop-in. Useful for plans that don't fully cover the class.
member-rate.see: Those members see the original price struck through next to theirs.
member-rate.check: Pick that plan's persona — the class row shows both prices.

class-pack.how: Add a one-time price with credits (e.g. 10) to a subscription type, optionally with a validity window. Each covered booking spends one credit; a cancelled booking refunds it.
class-pack.see: Members see their remaining credits; bookings say "1 credit".
class-pack.check: The pack persona has a "pack used up" switch to preview the empty state.

paid-trial.how: On a gated class, enable the trial door; leave the trial price empty for a free first class or set an amount to charge it. One trial per person, ever — enforced by email.
paid-trial.see: Newcomers get a "First time here" door at booking.
paid-trial.check: The Guest persona shows "trial available" on gated classes.

appointments.how: Appointments have no access gate: the price is the gate. Give each duration its own price (30/60/90 min), then optionally a member benefit — included with certain plans, a percentage off, or a fixed member price. Unpriced durations are free for everyone.
appointments.see: Clients pick a time and see exactly their price; covered members book free.
appointments.check: Each persona prices every duration on Offer → Pricing.

sell-course.how: Set a course's access to Sold and give it a price: buyers get lifetime access. Add a benefit so subscribers get it included or at a discount.
sell-course.see: It appears in your shop's Courses tab; owners watch it in their Space.
sell-course.check: Course rows in the price preview show each persona's price.

gift-cards.how: Enable gift cards and choose the amounts. Buyers receive a code by email; anyone can redeem it when paying for shop items, courses or drop-ins — partially or in full.
gift-cards.see: A Gift cards tab appears in your shop; checkouts get a "Have a gift card?" field.
gift-cards.check: The Payments page lists sold cards and balances.

no-show-fee.chip: Charge a fee after repeated no-shows
no-show-fee.how: Enable the no-show policy with a fee and a threshold (e.g. CHF 15 after 3). Strikes count automatically when you mark bookings as no-shows; at the threshold the member gets one fee with a payment link. You can always waive it.
no-show-fee.see: The member receives an email; you track and waive fees under Payments.
no-show-fee.check: Outstanding fees appear on the Payments page.

partner-pass.how: Create a subscription type with source Aggregator and set what the partner pays you per visit. Assign it to partner members and include it in the classes they may attend: each covered booking lands in a payout ledger instead of charging anyone.
partner-pass.see: Partner members book like regular members.

HowTo.faqTitle: Questions everyone asks at the start
HowTo.faqIntro: Meet Alex, who runs a small martial-arts studio. Six early questions, answered the way they play out for Alex.

q1.q: Can I let people book only specific classes?
q1.a: Alex sells a Beginners plan that should cover exactly two class types. In Linyup that is an access rule on the activity, not on the person: Alex sets both beginner activities to require a subscription that covers them, and leaves the open-mat activity open to everyone. Anyone on the Beginners plan can book those two classes — everything else politely refuses.

q2.q: What's the difference between an activity and a session?
q2.a: Alex offers 'Judo Fundamentals' once — that is the activity, the template. The calendar then holds many sessions of it: Monday 6 pm, Wednesday 7 pm, week after week. When Alex changes the activity's description or access rule, every future session follows; cancelling one rainy Monday touches only that single session.

q3.q: How do trial visitors end up in my contact list?
q3.a: Alex shares the studio's bio-link on Instagram. A visitor taps it, picks Thursday's trial session on the booking page and enters their name — Linyup creates the contact and the booking in one go. Next morning Alex finds them in Contacts, marked as a fresh lead, with the trial booking already attached.

q4.q: Does every member need a paid subscription?
q4.a: Alex's studio has paying adults, kids billed on paper invoices, and a retired co-founder who trains free forever. Only the adults hold subscriptions in Linyup. The others still get an affiliation — member — so they belong, show up in the right lists and can book members-only classes, with no billing attached.

q5.q: Do I need an appointment version of every class?
q5.a: Almost certainly not. Alex's head coach teaches kickboxing and functional workouts, and it is tempting to mirror each one as a separate private offering. But think about what is actually being sold: an hour of the coach's attention. The price and the length are the same either way — what happens in the hour is agreed on the day. So Alex creates ONE appointment activity, 'Personal training', and the coach publishes their availability against it. Make a second appointment activity only when it is genuinely a different product — a free 20-minute intro call next to a paid 60-minute session, say, because those differ in price and in who may book. That is the test: different terms, different offering. Same terms, one offering.

q6.q: What if I only want some of the public pages?
q6.a: Alex wants a bio-link and a booking page, but no shop yet. Public surfaces are plugins: Alex switches on the two that matter and leaves the rest off. Months later, when the first merch arrives, enabling the shop plugin simply adds it — nothing about the existing pages changes.

PromoCodes.entitiesHint: Leave everything unticked to include every item of the kinds you chose above.
PromoCodes.labelHint: Only you see this — for example “autumn flyer”.
PromoCodes.reservedHint: In checkout right now. These count toward the total until they are paid or expire.
PromoCodes.disableConfirm: Disable this code? Nobody can apply it any more. Checkouts already in progress still finish, and the record is kept.
PromoCodes.noDelete: Codes are never deleted — disabling one lets checkouts in progress finish and keeps the record.
PromoCodes.releaseReservationsConfirm: Free up every checkout currently holding this code? Use this when the code reports as fully used but nothing has sold. The number of paid uses does not change.
PromoCodes.clearRedemptionConfirm: Forget this person’s use of the code so they can apply it again. The total number of paid uses is unchanged.
PromoCodes.clearedToast: Done — they can use the code again.
PromoCodes.empty: No promo codes yet. Create one to run a campaign.
